text:
Aisha: Noticed multiple onboarding failures where rotated keys didn't get picked up in local dev loops. Root cause seems to be alias env vars + CLI caching.
Liam: Can you share the variants you're seeing?
Aisha: Found REDWOOD_API_KEY, RW_API_TOKEN, and legacy RED_KEY used in internal sample apps. Ops rotated the key in the console and the CLI still showed old user until restart.
Carlos: That's the caching we added in the session manager. It caches parsed creds for 10m to avoid repeated parsing. Good for long-running services, bad for quick env swaps.
Liam: Proposed fix: central env resolver that accepts aliases and a single-process deprecation log. Also change CLI to re-read env for env-sourced creds at each invocation (no long-lived cache).
Aisha: Also ask: whoami output confusing for project-scoped keys. It prints org only, so users think rotation didn't work. Should include scope info.
Carlos: Agree. We can show: org: acme, project: search-index (if present) and obfuscated key id. No raw tokens.
help-bot: created RW-912: add env alias resolver + CLI env re-read + whoami scope info (assignees: Carlos, Liam)
Liam: For SDK parity: make the resolver a small package (envauth) with API: getApiKey(), getProject(), with legacyAliases param. Implement in Node & Python first, then port.
Aisha: Docs note: add migration snippet for rotating short-lived keys in CI and local. Example: 
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=newkey
# restart CLI or ensure runner re-reads env
redwood whoami

Liam: Tests: make a tiny integration that flips env var mid-test and ensures next CLI invocation picks up the new value.
Carlos: I'll cut a patch to reduce cache scope and wire the alias resolver. Aim for patch release tonight.
Aisha: Thanks — this should reduce a lot of trial friction. Please ping when deployed.
